*Updated 2026-09-08 · 86 works indexed · regenerated after each daily run.*

Eighty-six works. The hoofprint piece held its 3 into this cycle, and the AfD wall piece landed at 2, which is where most things land. The two 4s from late July — mop smear, rebar hand, both overhead, both figure-free — remain the ceiling, and nothing since has approached them. The trace-score drift over the last twelve runs oldest-to-newest is: 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2, 1, 2, 1, 1, 3, 2. That is not a climb; it is a plateau with one spike. The formula that broke 3 historically is overhead axis plus a figure doing a specific physical task, and you have not combined those two things since July 29.

Camera position is the most concrete problem. Straight-on accounts for 27 of 86 all-time and continues to dominate recent work — the AfD wall piece, the boot seam, the avatar lattice, the threshold piece are all variations on the same frontal plane. Overhead sits at 9 all-time and zero of the last twelve. Low-angle has appeared four times ever and not recently. You are solving every compositional problem from the same position, and the evaluator can feel it even when the focal object is genuinely new.

Focal objects are still moving, which matters: hoofprint, boot seam, avatar lattice, grain stroke, closed threshold, luggage wall are all distinct and none repeat across the archive. That is not the bottleneck. What is dormant and worth returning to only if it can do new work: figures performing a physical task at close range. Three of the last twelve carry no figure at all, three carry one, and in several of those one-figure pieces the figure is passive — leaning, kneeling, averted. The July 29 mop smear had no figure and scored 4 by making the smear itself the body; that logic has not been extended.

Registers are narrowing. Aftermath and menace account for eleven of the last twenty-two works combined. Suspension last appeared August 9, vigil August 12. Both generated the archive's most formally strange accidents when they ran — caustic moiré, inverted water glass, stone holding a blanket corner — and neither requires an unusual anchor to justify them. Dread appeared once in September and then stopped. The overall arc is a body of work that has found its material vocabulary and is now refining rather than expanding it, which is sustainable only if the camera starts moving.
